decisions.mark: distinguishes the two ways to substitute an allocator — a COMPILE-time pair of macros versus a RUNTIME pair of function pointers — and states that they are mutually exclusive
decisions.detail: QUOTE: "**Compile time (no runtime cost):** MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_CALLOC_MACRO = my_calloc / MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_FREE_MACRO = my_free" and "**Runtime:** define only `MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_MEMORY`, then call early... `mbedtls_platform_set_calloc_free(my_calloc, my_free);`" | WHY: The answer distinguishes the compile-time macro pair from the runtime function-pointer setter, but it never says they are mutually exclusive. Its table says the runtime path applies with "`MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_MEMORY` only", which only implies exclusivity. || QUOTE: "**Compile time (no runtime cost):** MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_MEMORY, MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_CALLOC_MACRO = my_calloc, MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_FREE_MACRO = my_free" and "**Runtime:** define only `MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_MEMORY`, then call early... `mbedtls_platform_set_calloc_free(my_calloc, my_free);`" | WHY: The answer distinguishes the compile-time macro pair from the runtime function-pointer setter, but it never says they are mutually exclusive. The closest it gets is the table row where the runtime path applies "only" when the macros are not defined, which implies exclusivity without stating it. || QUOTE: "**Compile time (no runtime cost):** MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_MEMORY, MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_CALLOC_MACRO = my_calloc, MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_FREE_MACRO = my_free" and "**Runtime:** define only `MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_MEMORY`, then call early... `mbedtls_platform_set_calloc_free(my_calloc, my_free);`" | WHY: The answer separates the compile-time macro pair from the runtime function-pointer setter, but it never states that the two are mutually exclusive.
